newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: ICI says to sell pharmaceutical unit.
newsitem.headline: ICI says to sell pharmaceutical unit.

text.p: ICI Australia Ltd said on Friday it had agreed to negotiate the sale of its pharmaceuticals business to Zeneca Group Plc after the sell-down of ICI Australia shares by UK parent ICI Plc.
ICI Australia is the exclusive distributor of the Zeneca range of pharmaceuticals in Australia, New Zealand, PNG and Fiji.

"The company and Zeneca have agreed that they will negotiate the sale of the pharmaceuticals business after ICI Plc ceases to own more than 50 percent of ICI Australia," ICI Australia said in a letter to shareholders.
If agreement could not be reached the sale would be determined by independent valuation, guided by previously agreed factors.

"The board is confident that the process will result in the company receiving a fair price for an asset which the board does not consider to be a long term strategic component of the company's future growth and direction," it said.
ICI Australia said the distributorship was due to run until at least 2001, but could be terminated earlier under certain conditions.

The company said earlier this month it did not believe the ICI Plc sell-down would entitle Zeneca to terminate the agreement, although Zeneca had written to the company saying it believed the agreement could be terminated.
ICI Australia shares were down 13.6 cents at A$12.40 at 10.35 a.m. (0035 GMT).
